study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Fang et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2024
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities uncover two robust transdiagnostic biotypes

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: CNP (UCLA Consortium for Neuropsychiatric Phenomics) used as discovery dataset; COBRE (Center for Biomedical Research Excellence) used as validation dataset 1; DIRECT (site 20 of Depression Imaging Research Consortium) used as validation dataset 2; SALD (Southwest University Adult Lifespan Dataset, a single-site dataset) used for constructing normal structural covariance network (492 healthy individuals aged 19-80).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "The discovery dataset was obtained from the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) Consortium for Neuropsychiatric Phenomics (CNP)... The validation dataset 1 was obtained from the Centre for Biomedical Research Excellence (COBRE)... The validation dataset 2 was obtained from site 20 of the Depression Imaging Research Consortium (DIRECT)... To construct the normal structural covariance network, we utilized another extensive dataset from a single site (SALD), comprising 492 healthy individuals aged 19-80 years."

answer.CNP: Discovery dataset for normative model training (HCs) and patient subtyping (schizophrenia, BD, ADHD)

answer.COBRE: Validation dataset 1 for reproducibility analysis (schizophrenia patients and HCs)

answer.DIRECT: Validation dataset 2 for generalizability analysis (depression patients and HCs)

answer.SINGLE-SITE (SALD): Construction of normal structural covariance network (HCs only, not for normative modeling)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The study uses CNP as the primary discovery dataset where normative models are trained on healthy controls and applied to patients. COBRE serves as an independent validation dataset to test reproducibility in schizophrenia. DIRECT tests generalizability to an unseen psychiatric disorder (depression). SALD provides healthy individuals for constructing the structural covariance network used in disease epicenter analysis.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "A total of 496 patients with psychiatric disorders and 255 healthy controls (HCs) from three independent datasets (one discovery dataset and two validation datasets) were included in this study. Additionally, another extensive dataset comprising 492 healthy individuals aged 19-80 was included to construct a normal structural covariance network... we trained a Gaussian process regression model to estimate the normative range of regional gray matter volumes (GMVs) based on age and sex in HCs."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Fang2024.pdf.md: 2.1. Datasets, L72-L81; 2.2. Subtyping analysis, L84-L86

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The study constructs separate normative models for each dataset using healthy controls. For the discovery dataset (CNP), 110 HCs were used after exclusion (original 130). For validation dataset 1 (COBRE), 73 HCs were used. For validation dataset 2 (DIRECT), 251 HCs were used. The train/test split within each dataset is not reported. Note: SALD (492 HCs) was used only for structural covariance network construction, not for normative modeling.
